payload.rationale: The document is a sprint retro covering three load-bearing claims: async decision widget shipped, 23-point velocity, and Zephyr integration as key unlock. I expanded the existing Sample_Sprint4Retro_20260322 first so the passes can recognize potential duplication or continuation — the content and even the velocity figure are nearly identical to the March 22 retro. I expanded Position_ZephyrIntegrationUnlock, Obs_TinaVelocity, Obs_ZephyrRateLimitResolved, and StyleObs_Sprint4_MetricAnchor because they directly bind the document's specific claims (Zephyr unlock, 23-point velocity, metric-anchored style). I expanded Position_Sprint4ThesisProven and Obs_TanyaThesisProven because the shipped widget is the thesis-validation event Tanya frames. I expanded Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning and its three child positions (AntiPatternRealtimeChat, ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform, TargetMarketRemoteTeams) plus Position_PricingTwelveDollars because the async decision widget is the product thesis in action, and the passes need the full positioning frame to place this retro correctly within it. No areas were deliberately excluded — the document is short but touches sprint delivery, product thesis, integration dependencies, and positioning, all of which are covered.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.

positions.name: Sprint4DeliveryAccount
positions.frame: how do we account for what Sprint 4 delivered and what enabled it?
positions.why: All three expressions are confident, past-tense, realis claims about Sprint 4 outcomes — the deliverable (widget shipped), the performance metric (23-point velocity, highest this quarter), and the causal explanation (Zephyr integration as key unlock). They cohere as a single account of Sprint 4's delivery: what was shipped, at what velocity, and why that velocity was achievable. Internal tension is appropriate — src-1's communal 'we shipped' pools team effort while src-2's metric-anchored 'highest this quarter' performs a comparative achievement stance, but both are facets of the same delivery account read through the frame of 'what happened and what drove it.'

placements.why: All three segments thematically support the decision-capture-at-consensus narrative. src-1 reports shipping the async decision widget — the product embodiment of capturing decisions at the moment of consensus. src-3 identifies the Zephyr integration as the key unlock, i.e. the mechanism that enables cross-platform decision capture without separate plugins. src-2's velocity metric (23 points, highest this quarter) is a delivery fact that evidences successful execution of that capability. These are facts evidencing the narrative theme, not themes themselves — no new leaf is warranted.
